candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hemodialysis catheter hub disinfection
candidate.educational_objective: Prevent hemodialysis catheter-related bloodstream infection by disinfecting the catheter hub with an appropriate antiseptic before every access.

options.A: Disinfect the catheter hub with an appropriate antiseptic after removing the cap and before accessing the catheter.
options.B: Access the hub without disinfection if the catheter dressing is clean, dry, and intact.
options.C: Use clean technique instead of aseptic access because bloodstream-infection prevention applies only to fistulas and grafts.
options.D: Disinfect the catheter hub only once when the catheter is first inserted; repeat disinfection is unnecessary during later dialysis sessions.

candidate.rationale: CDC's current dialysis bloodstream-infection prevention Core Interventions instruct staff to scrub hemodialysis catheter hubs with an appropriate antiseptic after the cap is removed and before the catheter is accessed, every time it is accessed or disconnected. CDC also calls for staff education and competency in access care and aseptic technique. Therefore, A is correct. A clean dressing does not eliminate hub contamination risk, infection-prevention requirements apply to catheter access, and hub disinfection is repeated with each access rather than performed only at insertion.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports antiseptic disinfection of hemodialysis catheter hubs before every access as a core bloodstream-infection prevention practice.
candidate.source_document_title: Best Practices for Bloodstream Infection Prevention in the Dialysis Setting
candidate.source_locator: CDC Dialysis Safety → Core Interventions → 'Catheter hub disinfection': scrub catheter hubs with an appropriate antiseptic after the cap is removed and before accessing; perform every time the catheter is accessed or disconnected. 'Catheter/vascular access care observations' and 'Staff education and competency' also require adherence to aseptic technique for catheter access and access-care skills.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A nurse is preparing to access a client's hemodialysis central venous catheter. Which infection-prevention action is required each time the catheter is accessed?
